newsitem.title: JAPAN: British nuclear waste ship arrives in Japan.
newsitem.headline: British nuclear waste ship arrives in Japan.

text.p: A British ship carrying nuclear waste from France docked without incident at this northern Japanese port on Tuesday to jeers from anti-nuclear activists.

Escorted by two tug boats and six police helicopters flying overhead, the Pacific Teal ended an eight-week trip from the French port of Cherbourg that saw it sail past about 20 nations which protested against the voyage.

The ship's arrival coincides with a rise in anti-nuclear sentiment in Japan since a radiation leak from a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant last week that ranks as Japan's worst nuclear accident. The accident exposed 37 workers to radiation and revealed major safety flaws in the country's nuclear power industry.
Under the terms of an agreement between Japan, Britain and France, spent Japanese uranium fuel is reprocessed into plutonium and the waste is stored in Japan.

About 100 activists from environmental groups such as Greenpeace lined up on a road outside the harbour complex to protest against the ship's cargo, which includes radioactive material such as strontium.
